messages:
jon: quick heads-up — ran the mixed replay+synth load for json/toolcall validation and hit a p99 latency regression when JSON validation is enabled for funcalls. baseline (no-json-validate): p99=210ms; with-json-validate: p99=250ms. ~18% regression.

maria: ouch. can you share the run artifacts? is this consistent across model sizes / kv-cache warmup states? :thinking:

jon: attached in the run dir and CI artifacts from ci-bot below. it's reproducible on the 1k convo replay and synthetic steady-state. KV cache hit-rate matters a lot — cold start p99 is worse but steady-state still shows ~12% gap.

lee: interesting — did you let the kernel-selector do its dynamic picks? my hypothesis is kernel selection + small-batch JSON parsing overhead is shifting the sweet spot and causing different kernels to be chosen for tail workloads.

jon: yes dynamic kernel selection left on. i also tried forcing kernel to the fast attention path and the regression disappears (p99 ~212ms).

sam: can you paste the exact commands? i'll repro locally on my devbox.

jon: here are the commands i used:

```
# replay harness
./bench/replay --corpus=1k-replay.json --rps=120 --duration=900 --model=rw-7b --mode=toolcall-json-validate --kv-warmup=true --pin-kernel=auto

# forced kernel run
./bench/replay --corpus=1k-replay.json --rps=120 --duration=900 --model=rw-7b --mode=toolcall-json-validate --kv-warmup=true --pin-kernel=fast-attn
```

maria: thanks. two quick asks: (1) can we get the flamegraph + sampling profile for the with-validate p99 window? (2) capture the batch size distribution during the run (continuous batching histograms).

lee: i pulled the profile. major hot spots: JSON schema validation (sync) ~22% of CPU time during tail; kernel dispatch path (select_kernels) jumped to ~9% from ~3% in baseline. flamegraph link: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1782567890/flame.svg

jon: paste of the CPU stack sample (top lines):
```
parse_json_validate
parse_json_validate
dispatch_to_kernelselector
continuous_batcher::emit_batch
runtime_execute_attention
```

sam: so validates are happening inline in the request path. if the validation is sync and blocks the batching thread we can see smaller effective batches hitting the runtime which changes kernel choice. that matches the kernel-selector jump.

maria: two mitigation experiments to run: (A) move validation off the hot path onto a background validator + optimistic accept (with quick syntactic check inline), (B) add a short yield in validation to allow batching to collect. both are quick to prototype.

lee: i also want an apples-to-apples comparison with synthetic load (no replay) because replay has more burstiness. run where we: freeze kernel selection (--pin-kernel=fast-attn), freeze batching heuristics (--batcher-policy=static-32), toggle json-validate on/off. that isolates parsing cost.

jon: agreed. i've scheduled three runs in CI:
- 1782567891: replay, dynamic kernels, json-validate=on
- 1782567892: replay, pin-kernel=fast-attn, json-validate=on
- 1782567893: synth-steady, pin-kernel=fast-attn, json-validate=on/off pairs

ci-bot: CI artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/1782567890/results.tar.gz — includes latency histograms, batch-size CSVs, kv-hit heatmap, and profiler samples. :white_check_mark:

sam: nice. one more thing — check the retry logic in the client SDK. i saw retries spike in one run (50->80 retries/hour) when validation errors trigger a fallback path that does extra model calls. retries will also distort tail latency.

jon: good catch — the run i posted had the SDK set to validate+retry-on-fail. i'll re-run with retries disabled to separate validation cost from retry amplification.

maria: action items:
- jon: re-run the pinned-kernel + static-batcher experiments and upload artifacts (due EOD PST).
- lee: prototype background validation (branch bg-validate) and bench against pinned-kernel runs (PT).
- sam: reproduce locally and check SDK retry telemetry + KV warmup variance.

jon: will do. if bg validation reduces CPU for parse step and batch sizes grow back up we should see p99 revert. if not, we investigate kernel selector heuristics (maybe tweak selection thresholds to prefer faster-attn for small batches).

maria: thanks team. add notes to the perf board and we'll sync in tomorrow's perf sync. :thumbsup:

lee: +1. also leaving a quick note: when you upload results, include the exact kernel selection logs (they include the policy decision reasons) — that made debug faster for me.

jon: will include. thanks all. :rocket:
